item.title: Meteor hit Oklahoma 100 million years later than previously thought
item.description: Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin have rewritten a small part of Oklahoma's geologic history with global implications for ancient life. Below the surface of the small town of Ames, Oklahoma, a meteor impact site spans miles. The crater is buried by sedimentary strata in the subsurface, but it remains an important marker of Oklahoma's ancient past and present-day economy; the Ames impact structure is a major oil and gas producer. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A Texas oil geologist first saw McKittrick Canyon in 1921, later bought the land for a private retreat
item.description: In 1921, petroleum geologist Wallace Pratt was captivated by the stunning landscape of McKittrick Canyon. He subsequently partnered to acquire land which led to the establishment of family homes. Commencing in 1959, Pratt generously began donating his land for conservation, culminating in the 1972 creation of Guadalupe Mountains National Park. Today, his former residences stand preserved within the park, serving as valuable educational resources. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center.
